producer_report.summary:
Root cause: readings are not checked against the outcome the user observes. Structural terms and ambiguous ontology names stay undefined, and the work is built on a guess. The 7bf8 (ladder) and g6vy (publish) cases were already closed. The 0wtc misread (Hermes Agent versus the Orchestration god) was still open. I extended `check_defined_terms`, the existing gate for undefined terms, instead of adding a new step.

In `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs`:
- A new `AMBIGUOUS_NAMES: [&str; 1] = ["Hermes"]` sits beside `STRUCTURAL_TERMS`. One private `named_term` replaces `structural_term`. It matches a listed name as the exact word or its possessive, case-insensitively, and returns the ontology spelling, so the repair line reads `Term Hermes: <meaning of at least three words>`.
- The plain-prose filter is unchanged, so quoted spans, backticks, paths, identifiers, example lists and Athena-generated lines are still skipped.
- The error now says 'a structural term or an ambiguous name' and, for an ambiguous name, asks which recorded sense applies and to cite `docs/ontology.toml`.
- The doc comment names the root cause, the three jobs, 'covers 2 of the 3 cited jobs', `expected 2% of newly refused readings` and the one-sense limit. The `check_outcome_state` doc now says `check_defined_terms` catches both of the other two jobs.
- A test-only `UNGATED_TERMS` holds every other ontology term with a reason. The test `ambiguous_and_ungated_terms_cover_the_ontology` requires each `[[term]]` of `docs/ontology.toml` to be in exactly one of the two lists, and each listed name to be an ontology term. Adding an ontology term now fails the build until someone decides whether readings must define it. Controls show each fault is reported.

In `crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs`: I wrote the corpus tests first and ran them against the unchanged source; four tests failed (listed in `checks_run`). The 0wtc request is now `REQUEST_0WTC`. The replay tests assert 2 of 3, refusal naming Hermes, acceptance with a three-word `Term Hermes:` line, and refusal of a one-word meaning. There are 10 new `ambiguous-name-*` cases, including the real approval and root-cause generators, `INPUT_FORMS` grows to 41, and a new test checks the CHANGELOG and D165 text.

CHANGELOG.md: I corrected the two unreleased bullets in place. docs/decisions.md: D165 is appended and nothing above it changed; it revises D164's scope sentence and its 3% share and records the one-sense limit.

The full test run, fmt, clippy and the policy scan pass. The rest-of-workspace run first failed on the backtest, which I fixed (see `mistakes`).

checks_run.command: cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus (BEFORE touching reading.rs, CHANGELOG.md or docs/decisions.md)
checks_run.note: Failed as planned: ambiguous_name_changelog_and_decision, defined_terms_replay_over_the_cited_jobs, delivery_verb_replay_over_the_cited_jobs and corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome (the new Refuse cases for the 0wtc request, the possessive, the lowercase use, the acceptance bullet and the approval title were accepted). 16 others passed.

checks_run.command: cargo test -q -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus (after the change)
checks_run.note: 20 passed, 0 failed, rerun after the final D165 wording.
1141 passed, 1 ignored (unit tests), plus the integration tests, all green. Run before the D165 rewording; the tests that read docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md were rerun after it.
10 passed after the final wording edits.

First run failed: athena-cli backtest the_real_log_has_no_condition_a_finding_against_the_confirmed_list. D165 used the phrase 'amends D164', and the backtest reads that as an unconfirmed supersession hit. Reworded to 'revises D164's scope sentence'. Second run: every test binary passed.
17 passed, rerun after the final edits. No banned word in the changed files.
No output; run after the final edits.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`: a test replays the recorded request of 20261017-173508-0wtc through `refusing_check` with a reading that has no `Term Hermes:` assumption and asserts check_defined_terms refuses it naming Hermes; the same reading with a `Term Hermes:` line of three or more words is accepted. The test fails on the code before the change.
criteria_check.evidence: defined_terms_replay_over_the_cited_jobs now takes REQUEST_0WTC, calls refusing_check on base_reading, expects Some(("check_defined_terms", e)) with Hermes and `Term Hermes:` in e, accepts it with 'Term Hermes: the studied self-improving agent, not part of Athena', and refuses 'Term Hermes: agent'. The corpus cases ambiguous-name-hermes-undefined-in-0wtc-request (Refuse) and ambiguous-name-hermes-defined-is-accepted (Accept) cover the same. Before the change the run failed defined_terms_replay_over_the_cited_jobs, delivery_verb_replay_over_the_cited_jobs and corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome; after it all 20 tests pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`: the replay over the three cited jobs now asserts check_defined_terms catches 2 of 3 (7bf8 and 0wtc), check_outcome_state still catches g6vy, and CHANGELOG.md states the same counts.
criteria_check.evidence: defined_terms_replay_over_the_cited_jobs asserts caught == [7bf8, 0wtc] ('of 3'). delivery_verb_replay_over_the_cited_jobs asserts check_outcome_state catches exactly g6vy, and the 7bf8 and 0wtc requests are refused by check_defined_terms. Both tests read the normalised CHANGELOG.md and require 'check_defined_terms covers 2 of the 3 cited jobs', 'covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs', 'are not caught by this check', all three job ids, and no '3 of the 3 cited jobs'. criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: cases show the class, not one job: other requests using Hermes in plain prose are refused, while Hermes inside quotes, backticks, paths or Athena-generated lines (root-cause and approval requests) is not, and a request with no listed name is unchanged.
criteria_check.evidence: Unit test defined_terms_refuses_an_ambiguous_ontology_name refuses Hermes, Hermes's, hermes, HERMES, a bullet and a bare 'Hermes'. It accepts double, curly, single and backtick quotes, example lists, fenced code, docs/hermes.md, hermes_notes, Hermes::new, hermeshub, Hermesian and a request with no listed name. Corpus cases cover the approval source (accepted), the approval title (refused), the root-cause introspection line (accepted), the possessive, lowercase, bullet, quoted/path/identifier and inside-other-words requests. Full `cargo test -q -p athena-core` passed.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: a test reads docs/ontology.toml and fails if any name on the ambiguous-name list in reading.rs is not a `[[term]]` name there.
criteria_check.evidence: ambiguous_and_ungated_terms_cover_the_ontology parses docs/ontology.toml with crate::mirrors::parse_ontology(include_str!) and compares AMBIGUOUS_NAMES and the cfg(test) UNGATED_TERMS with the term names in both directions. It requires an empty problem list for the real data. Controls: a listed 'Zeus', an ontology name 'Zeus' in neither list, a name in both lists, a short reason, a lowercase name and an empty list each report a problem. Passes.

The error now reads 'as a structural term or an ambiguous name', asks which recorded sense applies and to cite docs/ontology.toml. criteria_check.evidence: The existing unreleased check_defined_terms bullet was corrected in place. It names the root cause, the three job ids, and says check_outcome_state and check_governance_coverage cover 20261014-082328-g6vy while check_defined_terms covers 2 of the 3 (7bf8, 0wtc). criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test`: all pass with no new warnings.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I also ran them: `cargo fmt --all --check` passed with no output, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` finished clean, and the athena-core and rest-of-workspace test runs passed (see checks_run).

open_issues: The check forces a restatement of the name but cannot verify that a `Term Hermes:` line matches the two recorded senses. The doc comment, CHANGELOG and D165 state this limit; it is not hidden.
The 2% share is an estimate; the loop replay at verification measures the real share. Narrowing is a one-element edit of AMBIGUOUS_NAMES.

D164 stays byte-for-byte as the append-only rule requires, so its text still says 20261017-173508-0wtc is caught by no check and its share is 3%. D165 revises both, and the CHANGELOG, the doc comment and the tests carry the current figures.
docs/decision-links.toml was not touched: D165 avoids the phrase 'amends', so D164 is not marked amended by D165 in the decision view. If the owner wants that link, they confirm it in the list.
mistakes: D165 first said 'amends D164', which the athena-cli backtest read as an unconfirmed supersession hit and failed. The full-workspace run caught it. I reworded D165 and the corpus needle.
The first rustfmt-unformatted edits to reading.rs and refusal_corpus.rs were fixed by cargo fmt --all before any check.
learnings: The athena-cli backtest test (the_real_log_has_no_condition_a_finding_against_the_confirmed_list) scans docs/decisions.md for the phrases 'amends', 'supersedes' and 'superseded by' followed by a decision id. Each hit must be listed in docs/decision-links.toml, the list the owner confirms. A new decision that uses 'amends D164' fails that test, so D165 says 'revises D164's scope sentence'.

check_defined_terms ran its words through request_words, which lowercases and keeps 's as part of a word. A bare name match therefore needs only an exact lowercase comparison plus the possessive strip; no plural stem is needed.
parse_ontology(include_str!("../../../docs/ontology.toml")) works from reading.rs tests and gives the seven term names: planning, job, Athena, Hermes, product versus system, landed, Sri.
The Read tool refuses docs/decisions.md in full (381 KB); use offsets.
desires: A rustdoc or script to list the phrase triggers that crates/athena-cli/src/backtest.rs reads from the decision log (amends, supersedes, superseded by) would have saved a failed run. Neither the brief nor the plan mentioned that 'amends D164' needs a confirmed link in docs/decision-links.toml.
